claims.text: The HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure contains nano- to micro-scale interfaces and phase domains.
A machine-learning model using multiscale heterostructure descriptors and DFT-derived interaction data can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior of HfNbTiVAl10.
Microstructural descriptors obtained from microscopy and EBSD can be integrated with atomic-level DFT interaction data in a mechanical-property prediction framework.
DFT-calculated atomic interactions can inform descriptors relevant to phase distribution and local stiffness.
The hierarchical heterostructure influences local stiffness in HfNbTiVAl10.
The hierarchical heterostructure alters stress distribution in HfNbTiVAl10.
Interfaces in the hierarchical heterostructure influence the initiation of plastic deformation and fracture.
Microstructure-derived descriptors capture variations in local elastic properties.
Microstructure-derived descriptors capture local yield-initiation thresholds.
Microstructure-derived descriptors identify potential fracture-initiation sites.
Combining microstructural descriptors with DFT-derived data can predict macroscopic mechanical behavior more efficiently than simulations that explicitly resolve every microstructural detail.
The proposed model will improve the accuracy of Young's-modulus, yield-strength, and fracture-toughness predictions by 10–20% relative to established simulations.
The proposed model will reduce computation time by roughly one order of magnitude relative to established simulations.
Full-scale DFT, molecular-dynamics, and multiscale continuum approaches require extensive computational resources and time for the proposed task.
Predictive improvements may fail when the descriptors omit mechanically relevant hierarchical features.
Predictive improvements may fail under deformation mechanisms arising at temperatures or strain rates outside the modeled conditions.
Predictive improvements may fail for heterostructures outside the model's training-data distribution.
